cells.quote: The multiagent framework outperformed single-LLM baselines across multiple evaluation settings, achieving high information accuracy and role-playing scores under standardized dialogue conditions. However, limited discriminative power against specific leading questions on low-quality inquiries indicated that while these findings specifically establish high fidelity under structured conditions, further adaptation is required for authentic student interactions. In assessments using standard dialogue scripts, the Qwen3-32B–based framework attained the highest role-playing competency score of 39.67 (SD 0.71) and received high expert praise.
cells.note: The study reports a benchmark comparison rather than random assignment; the learners' prior knowledge and training setting were not stated.
